newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends sluggish session mixed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends sluggish session mixed.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures tightly mixed in subdued trade Monday, with nearby contracts managing to edge higher after posting losses the last six consecutive sessions.

Dealers said much of the day's activity was technically driven, with mixed short covering and light industry-related buying accounting for most of the gains. But producer selling overhead limited the upturn and confined prices to a narrow range, traders said.
March delivery rose $3 a tonne on the day, to $1,336, after ranging between $1,340 to $1,331. Second-month May firmed $2 to $1,360, while the back months finished up $2 to down $3.
Turnover was thin at an estimated 4,224 lots, down sharply from Friday's official tally of 14,595 lots.

On the charts, traders pegged March near-term resistance at $1,350, then $1,358-$1,360. Support was seen at today's low of $1,331, a double bottom on the charts. The next downside target was put at $1,322, March's life-of-contract low.
Traders said the slow pace of arrivals out of Ghana and Ivory Coast was viewed as supportive to the futures market and could point to a smaller West African harvest this season.
The Ghana Cocoa Board said on Monday cumulative Ghana purchases by December 19, 1996 totalled 184,034 tonnes compared with 259,718 by December 21, 1995.

Meanwhile, trade house General Cocoa said in a weekly report total cumulative Ivory Coast cocoa arrivals were "guesstimated" at some 580,000 tonnes through January 4, compared with an estimated 717,000 tonnes at the same time last year.

Elsewhere, the Brazilian Trade Commission Comcauba said Monday Bahia 1996/97 cocoa arrivals totalled 2,579,089 million 60-kg bags by the week ending January 5 compared with 2,209,217 bags by January 7 last year.
